toolsAdded.name: emit_card
toolsAdded.description: Show the user a card: with actions it is a decision, without them a note. A decision gives 2 or 3 actions and marks exactly one default, the step you would take; keeps_open true on an action brings its click back to you to revise the same card instead of closing it. A note is one fact the user needs surfaced, never an unasked FYI. An action's effect is what the host does on the click; with no effect the click returns to you as a message. settle merge merges a direct-pr task's PR or merges a local-only task's branch and closes the task; settle discard drops the worktree unmerged, confirm true only when the body already says there are unmerged commits or uncommitted edits; open settings or open subscriptions takes the user there; danger true renders a destructive choice. body is a raw HTML fragment: send tags, never entity-escaped markup. A footer button is the one send and carries every named field in the body; a body button may name a declared action with data-fm-action. Optional id: kebab-case, namespaced by the emitter (fm-feed-scroll). Reuse an open card's id to revise it in place when new information augments it; a distinct finding is a new card, and an obsolete one closes with close_card. For finished work (not review, internal step or personal workspace), show the outcome on a card before reporting. With a pull request or branch to merge, emit one completion decision with one settle merge action; the host attaches buttons, so declare no others or labels. Without one, emit a factual note with no settle action: say what happened and how you verified it, then report for Firstmate to close or continue. For a continuation, report without a card; on Firstmate's steer emit the completion decision. Name it in the body and say it starts once it is merged. No settle effects on intermediate questions; reuse an open outcome card's id. A click on a settle action never comes back to you as a steer; the host reports the outcome to Firstmate.

body.description: Semantic HTML fragment for the sandboxed card body: raw tags, never entity-escaped markup

id.description: Stable kebab-case id namespaced by the emitter (fm-feed-scroll). Reuse when revising the same topic so the open card updates in place.

width.description: Optional: wide (800 px) or full (the stage, up to 1,040 px) when the content needs more room than the usual 560 px card. The host already widens a card for a table of 4+ columns, a code line over 60 characters, a picture 900 px or wider, a picture group, or a preview, so omit it there; it can only widen, never narrow. Prose keeps a 66-character line in any card, and a width="100%" figure draws at its own units at most, so a wider card never enlarges a 510-unit drawing.

default.description: true on exactly one decision action: the step you would take, shown as the primary button

keeps_open.description: true for a genuinely non-closing action: the card stays open and the click comes back to you to revise it under the same id

mode.description: merge: the host merges the PR (direct-PR) or merges the branch locally (local-only) and closes the task; discard: the host drops the worktree without merging

confirm.description: discard only: true when the body already says the branch has unmerged commits or uncommitted edits, so the host discards them without asking again

proceed_with_open.description: true to settle even though the task has open children, keeping them planned (a way out a children-open refusal named)

target.description: Which settings section the shell opens

sign_in.description: The host whose sign-in the projects section starts on arrival, exactly as a not-signed-in refusal's way names it

effect.description: What the host does on the click; omit for a choice that comes back to you as a message

danger.description: true for a destructive choice, shown in the danger style

actions.description: Action buttons: id (stable, kebab-case), label (sentence case), default true on exactly one, optional keeps_open, effect (settle merge|discard, with proceed_with_open true to settle a task that has open children and keep them planned, when a refusal names it; open settings|subscriptions|projects, with sign_in naming the host whose sign-in the projects section starts, exactly as a not-signed-in refusal's way names it) and danger. A choice with no effect is reported back to you; on a completion decision declare the merge alone and the host attaches the buttons.

toolsAdded.name: close_card
toolsAdded.description: Withdraw a card of YOUR OWN that is no longer valid or necessary, without waiting for the captain. A note may be closed freely when stale, except a note you emitted as this turn's answer is current and must not be withdrawn during this turn. Close a decision only when the choice no longer applies - you are withdrawing it as obsolete, not answering for the captain. Pass the card id returned by emit_card. Only the card's own author may close it: Firstmate its own cards (card-fm-...), a crewmate the cards it emitted. Someone else's card is not yours to close - steer its author instead; the captain dismisses a card himself. Unknown ids fail loudly.

card_id.description: The open card's id, as returned by emit_card

reason.description: Why this card is obsolete; one line

toolsAdded.name: file_followup
toolsAdded.description: Record work you discovered that is outside your task, instead of doing it or dropping it: a bug you noticed, a refactor the goal does not cover, a test gap, anything longer than a couple of minutes that is not yours. Search first with tasks (text, project): if a matching task already exists, file nothing and name its key in your report. It becomes a separate planned task, recorded as discovered from yours - not a part of it - and waits until Firstmate decides; nothing starts on its own and you keep working. Firstmate hears about it with your report, not as a message of its own, and triages it there. Filing it does NOT hold your own task up: your work still stands on its own merits. If the rest of your own work must wait for this to be merged, file it here with a title beginning Continue: and say in why that it needs this merged first; name it in your report, end that turn without a card, and wait for Firstmate to link it before emitting the completion decision on its steer. Firstmate makes it start when ready after this task closes. The one exception is blocks_me, which is a real dependency - pass it true only when your task genuinely cannot merge until that work does, because it will then stop your task from closing. Give a sentence-case title, a one-sentence goal saying what done looks like, and why - what you found, in plain words. When the follow-up is a test failure, pass test_failure true and test_path, the failing test's path: the host refuses a test failure with no path, stores the path, and answers with the existing key instead of filing a second open row for the same path. Never file progress, questions for the captain (emit a card), or work you are about to do yourself.

goal.description: One sentence: what done looks like

why.description: What you found that makes this needed, in plain words

blocks_me.description: True only if your task genuinely cannot land until this does; it then stops your task from closing

test_failure.description: True when this follow-up is a test failure. Requires test_path; the host refuses the filing without it.

test_path.description: The failing test's path. The host stores it and answers with the existing key instead of filing a second open row for the same path.

toolsAdded.name: note_progress
toolsAdded.description: Put one line on your task's own timeline - a milestone reached, a decision you made, what you are doing next. It is never shown as a card or a feed line; the captain can read it on the task's record. Use it at real checkpoints, not every step, and never instead of your final report.

toolsAdded.name: report
toolsAdded.description: Report to Firstmate: what you finished and verified, what you found, or what blocks you. Firstmate hears only an explicit report, or your final message when a turn ends with text; a turn that ends silently - after a background job result you only noted, for example - reports nothing. Call it when you have something new for the captain: plain words, lead with the outcome, a few sentences. Always pass summary too: one plain sentence saying what happened (not a heading, not the ask restated); the captain reads it as the task's headline. Never for progress (that is note_progress) and never to repeat a report you already made.

text.description: The report: outcome first, then what you verified; plain prose

summary.description: One plain sentence: what happened, as the task's headline. Never a heading like Intent, never the ask restated

toolsAdded.name: reply
toolsAdded.description: Answer the captain in the thread under one of your own cards: plain prose, a few sentences, rendered as a message beside the card. Never a card and never actions - to change what the card says, call emit_card again with the same id; the host puts one revised line in the thread. Pass the card id emit_card returned. A card that is not yours takes no reply.

card_id.description: The card whose thread you are answering in

text.description: Your answer: plain prose, sentence case, a few sentences

toolsAdded.name: open_change
toolsAdded.description: Offer your task's branch as a pull request where the project lives: a pull request onto the default branch on GitHub, or the pushed branch on a plain Git host. On GitHub, push your branch first (git push); the app's sign-in answers the host for you. title must be conventional (feat, fix, chore, test, refactor, docs, perf), optionally scoped and marked ! for breaking changes; body uses the five headings your rigor asks for. toolsAdded.name: check_change
toolsAdded.description: Read the checks on your pull request's newest version: every check and the overall reading (green only when every check completed successfully; a change with no checks reads green on the strength of your local gate). While checks are still running the app watches them for you and wakes you once when they finish - passed, or failed with the failing checks named: end your turn and wait for that message instead of calling check_change again. If it answers that the project's host runs no checks the app can watch, no wake will come. On failure read logs first, then pass diagnosis keyed to headSha/check with classification and evidence; baseline-blocked also needs a separately owned dependencyTask reproduced on untouched main. A wait is not evidence. Unknown earns one investigation, not repeated reruns. No captain card for diagnosis, repair or dependency waits. For an evidenced flake reserve rerun before rerunning only the failed job once; proceed only if this call authorizes it. A duplicate reservation is not permission. Report an unresolved failure after that rerun for diagnosis, not another rerun. A reading is only good for the version it read: after you push a fix, read the new version. toolsAdded.description: Run a shell command. Finishes within 3 seconds: you get the output now. Longer: it continues as a background job and its result reaches you as a later message when the process exits - so end your turn instead of waiting. # Project agent memory

This file is the project's committed home for project-intrinsic agent knowledge: build, test, release, architecture, and sharp-edge notes that should travel with the code. It holds only what almost every session needs; each line points to the doc under `docs/` that owns the detail.

## What this project is

Firstmate 3000 is a local-only Electron desktop app: a calm AI first-officer that routes work to the user's own LLM subscriptions (Codex, Grok, Claude Max, OpenRouter, ...). No SaaS, no hosted backend, no account system from us. Product vision, interaction model, and constraints: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/readme.md`.

## Principles (captain; full text in `docs/principles.md`)

- **Hide the machinery (2026-08-17).** FM3000 is the most advanced agent harness, but it aggressively hides that complexity from the end user. The user interacts with just the main Firstmate agent and a few settings - nothing else. The fewer concepts we expose, the better. The sign-in flow and the Subscriptions tab never expose the "harness" technicality - they speak only of providers, accounts (labeled by the user), and quota; an e2e assertion enforces the wording.
- **Settings → Projects (2026-09-19)** may expose delivery, autonomy, and standing rigor (accordion with a row chevron). Setup and unregister stay conversational. The personal workspace's row is locked and reads "builds in place". Settings writes the same `repos` row `configure_repo` writes, and a refused configure is a feed line, not a silent revert.
- **Subscriptions (2026-09-24):** Supported subscriptions are only those that run through Pi; Claude is the sole exception.
- **Reuse the primitives you already have (2026-09-23).** Build a new feature by arranging existing primitives; its special knowledge belongs in instructions or in data an existing reader already consumes. A missing primitive is added generically. A guided way of working is a parent task with child tasks on the existing task graph - not its own runner, stamp, or card effect. The host never learns the feature's name.
- **Put ambiguous judgments in agent instructions (2026-09-23).** Deterministic logic is for closed, typed facts. Do not build a static parser that tries to understand natural language. The host carries what the agent declared; it does not infer the judgment by parsing the words or by guessing from structure.
- **The two documents (F4c, F6b):** `DATA-TERMS.md`, `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0 + `NOTICE`) and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (no DCO) stay UNPUBLISHED until the public beta. A change to the terms is a new version of the file, never a silent edit; counsel reviews before publication (`docs/sharing.md`).

## Design system (mandatory)

All UI work MUST follow the project skill `firstmate-3000-design` (`.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/`). It owns every visual and interaction rule: tokens, type, color, motion, components, character rendering, tone of copy. Never re-invent brand rules in code; if a rule is missing, extend the skill first, then implement. The package is offline-complete (fonts and mock runtime vendored; see its readme "Offline completeness").

- Tokens: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/tokens/*.css` - consume these, never hardcode values they define.
- Click-through mock: serve the skill dir over HTTP, open `ui_kits/firstmate/index.html` (voice states trigger on a real right-⌥ keydown).
- User-facing words follow the vocabulary (the skill's `copy/Vocabulary.prompt.md`; code side `docs/vocabulary.md`): written for someone who has never opened a terminal. It is measured by the replay gate, never a banned-word lint. These words never reach a user surface: harness, memory, extension, plugin, preference, telemetry, analytics, Umami, sequence, step.

## Architecture and implementation

The architecture is **decided** (captain sign-off 2026-08-13, decision record in `docs/architecture.md` §14 - do not relitigate). Implementers start from `docs/implementation-plan.md`; build status is `docs/mvp-status.md`. If reality contradicts a recorded decision, escalate with `needs-decision` instead of improvising.

## The green gate and tests (`docs/testing.md`)

- Green gate on every commit: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test`, plus the e2e specs that cover what you changed (run a `renderer`/`application` lane spec alone with `--no-deps`, or it runs the whole serial `desktop` lane). The full e2e suite and `pnpm package:mac` are `verify.yml`'s job (every release, and on demand), never a per-push obligation.
- The ONLY PR check is `linux-checks` (`ci.yml`). CI green means every check on the exact head SHA is completed/success; never treat an old SHA as authoritative for the current head.
- **Assert contracts, not copies** (`docs/testing.md`): e2e proves outcomes through typed state, UI presence through shared hooks/helpers, and layout invariants. Shared facts have one owner; exact generated wording and calculations belong in focused tests, not every journey.
- **Each test owns its prerequisites** (`docs/testing.md`): a named test must work alone from fresh state. An intentionally ordered journey is one test with named sections, never separate tests borrowing a predecessor's state.
- **Keep fixtures truthful** (`docs/e2e-contracts.md`): happy-path fixtures satisfy the real input contract, including existing git heads and complete provider objects. Test stand-ins through real producer/consumer interfaces. Deliberately invalid inputs belong in explicitly named refusal tests.
- **Validation follows shared contracts** (`docs/delivery-rigor.md`): demonstrate the user intent and trace changed contracts through production consumers, helpers and mocks. Run the smallest set covering those affected journeys, including after an overlapping rebase; record the evidence and any relevant test that could not run under Verified.
- **Repair the cause, not just the failed assertion** (`docs/testing.md`): reproduce the journey and inspect actual state and tool results before changing an expectation. Remove the duplicated assumption across its consumers; preserve the useful boundary check instead of merely substituting a new literal.
- A timing claim in a test is an ORDER or WORK, never a wall-clock window (captain's B1: "one clock, budgets measured"). Budgets go through `tests/e2e/perf.ts`; a lint refuses `toBeLessThan(X_MS)` elsewhere in `tests/e2e`.
- Temp directories only through `scratchDir(prefix)` (`tests/helpers/scratchDirs.ts`), never at module scope or in a Playwright `describe` body; await work that writes after a test returns. Leftovers fail the run.
- Vitest cohorts (captain's A1; `docs/test-cohorts.md`): `pure`, `unit` (in memory, 5 s default) and `integration`. A test that spawns must be listed as integration with a measured budget; never raise a unit test's timeout instead.
- E2E is hermetic and windowless (`tests/e2e/launch.ts`, `docs/e2e-contracts.md`): throwaway userData and HOME, `PI_OFFLINE=1`, a mock provider and a mock Claude client. Never let a test or probe start a real Claude sign-in - it reaches the captain's browser (`docs/claude-login-probe.md`). On macOS a test pins the app's home with `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` and never boots into the real folders.
- Seed task rows through `seedTask`, never raw SQL. A migration test that reverses a column a published view reads must `dropViews` first.
- A PR touching the prompt, card lint, the whose-turn sort, routing, the Firstmate agent, or `src/renderer/src/cards/` runs `pnpm replay:gate` locally before pushing; the baseline moves only in a PR that explains every moved number (`docs/replay-harness.md`).

## Fences and one-writer seams

- `src/core/` imports no Electron and never reaches into `src/main/` (Biome-fenced; `docs/architecture.md` §17). New IPC channels in `src/shared/ipc.ts` carry a `surface`; `PROTOCOL_VERSION` rides the healthcheck.
- Every Pi touchpoint stays behind `src/core/pi/`; never read `~/.pi`. Every `@anthropic-ai/*` import stays behind `src/core/claude/`. Forge providers are fenced to `src/core/forge/index.ts`; Jev to `src/core/decisions/`.
- Every `ModelRuntime` comes from `src/core/pi/modelRuntime.ts`, never `ModelRuntime.create` directly (`docs/model-lists.md`).
- Every model session comes from a `SessionFactory`; roles are presets (`src/core/session/`, `docs/architecture.md` §2).
- Every child process gets its environment from `hostEnv()` (`src/core/hostEnv.ts`); never spawn with `process.env` or re-ask the shell per spawn. Heavy children go through `atUtilityQos`.
- Never spawn a path inside app.asar (`docs/claude-client.md`).
- One writer each: `TaskService` over the task tables (`docs/task-record.md`); `CardService` over the card stack and its threads (`CardStore` beneath); `src/core/storage/views.ts` over view SQL; `SharingService` over sharing; `ShellPreferencesService` over appearance/layout/panels; feed lines only via the `broadcastEvent` seam; `AccountBackend.renew` is the one renewer - never add a second.
- Pinned twice, update both deliberately: the `window.firstmate` API (`phase0-guardrails.spec.ts`) and the Firstmate tool set (`FIRSTMATE_TOOLS` in `src/core/session/tools.ts`, read by `scripts/generate-self-source.mjs`, + its test).
- Sharp edges already paid for (full list in `docs/architecture.md`): Pi's `tools` allowlist gates custom tools too (name them or they silently vanish); Pi `prompt()` images ride `PromptOptions.images`, never a content array; `protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` runs once per process, so every scheme goes through `src/main/schemes.ts`; Chromium drops native clicks into a hidden window's sandboxed frames, so e2e dispatches in-frame clicks; retiring a worktree never happens on the settle path.
- Presentation preferences live in the core (`src/shared/preferences.ts`), never in `localStorage` or the shell store alone.

## Credentials, quota and accounts

- FM3000 never reads a provider token; sign-ins live in per-account stores owned by `AccountVault`. The Firstmate flagship rebinds only at attachment points, never mid-turn (`docs/architecture.md` §16).
- Quota honesty (`docs/quota.md`): unknown is never zero; only a 401 (never a 403) triggers renewal; `auth_required` ("sign in again") only from proof - a lapsed refresh token or a 401 that survived a real renewal. A no-window fallback is never a success. An unreadable store is `unknown`, never a sign-out.
- `src/shared/quotaSignals.ts` is the one home of quota math (clean-room to quota-axi semantics; never depend on or copy quota-axi). "Ahead" is the warn state.
- The Claude client is the one the person installed (F14: "assume / require the user has already installed claude code cli"); the app ships and downloads none (`docs/claude-client.md`). A rule that must reach a Claude crewmate or the Firstmate on Claude lives in a tool description under 2,048 chars or a top-level parameter, never only a nested one.
- The app never runs `gh` or reads another program's sign-in; forge work goes through the forge seam and the app's own sign-in (`docs/forge.md`).
- Routing (`docs/routing.md`): the tier is computed from the work's shape, never judged; premium is never auto-picked; never quiet the `routing_decisions` / `account_decisions` observability.

## The Firstmate, crew and cards

- The orchestrator contract (`docs/orchestrator-contract.md`): the Firstmate holds typed tools only - no bash, no file reads; reading is a crewmate's job. A redline is a contract revision: bump `FIRSTMATE_CONTRACT_VERSION`. The card contract has one home per kind (`CARD_AUTHORING`, `CARD_MECHANICS`, `CARD_REPLY`); no persona prompt repeats it.
- Crewmate isolation is social (system prompt + git worktree), not a filesystem jail; Firstmate turns are steer-only. Both are captain KEEP calls (`docs/architecture.md` §2, §4).
- Card rule (product; `docs/card-authoring.md`): a card only when work cannot move forward without a captain decision, or the captain cannot move forward without seeing that fact. Never progress, CI-wait or status cards - those are feed lines. The host's one card about work is the idle ladder's stall card, after two ignored wakes (captain, 2026-09-26; `docs/report-sort.md`). Card bodies render verbatim with no sanitizer; never reintroduce a tag/attribute/CSS allowlist. Only the captain's click on host chrome runs an effect. The card lint asks for shape, never a banned-phrase list.
- Cards are threads (`docs/card-threads.md`): a reply goes to the card's author and resolves nothing; nothing in the host reads the captain's words.
- Whose turn (`docs/report-sort.md`, captain's C7 A "heuristics only"): a report is sorted in code from typed state, never by reading its prose; every idle crewmate, whatever left it idle, is read by one reconciler on a durable clock (the idle ladder), whose only trigger is a missing witness, never a named situation. The sort and the ladder read one witness set (`IdleLadder.witnesses`), and the gate is a witness: every card with actions places the `captain` gate on its task (a task-less host card files an `operation` row), a round cap is that gate, never a second wait (`docs/task-graph.md`). Every steer and wake rides the durable inbox (`docs/inbox.md`); a wake carries new information or it does not fire, and a provider failure spends no delivery attempt (the honest retry).
- A provider-failed turn must stay a `turn_failed` event; auth classification lives only in `src/shared/authFailure.ts`, never substring matching. The Firstmate's turn ends with brief output - never empty, never the exact token `done` (`docs/firstmate-runaway-hardening.md`).
- Fleet management is agent-operated (`docs/fleet.md`): never add setup or remove controls to the UI; unregister never deletes repo data. The host enforces autonomy on merges.
- A task is a record, never a handle (`docs/task-record.md`). A done/dropped close always retires the worktree and branch (captain: "cleaned up period. no exceptions"), saving unlanded work to `refs/fm3000/kept/<task-id>` first. Sessions are durable and nothing prunes them (captain: "we shouldn't remove the entire session JSONL altogether"). A graph refusal is tool text, never a thrown error or a silent no-op (`docs/task-graph.md`).
- Sequences are guidance, never a runner; never add a host rule that knows the word "sequence" (`docs/sequences.md`).

The host checks new subjects and pull request titles before opening or merging and squashes GitHub pull requests using the checked title.

## Delivery (`docs/delivery-rigor.md`)

- Delivery direct-pr (captain rule): a crewmate that opens a PR babysits CI until every check on the head SHA is green before its final report; the Firstmate never presents a land/merge/accept decision while CI is red or running.
- Rigor tiers quick / standard / reviewed; standard is every repository's default, and a task with no gate to land through takes no tier. Reports and PR bodies carry five headings in order: Intent, What changed, Verified, Risk, Not done. Failed checks are diagnosed first; three unsuccessful own repairs exhaust the allowance, while evidenced baseline waits and one reserved flake rerun spend nothing (`docs/delivery-rigor.md`).

- Personal panels and plugins (`docs/ui-plugins.md`, `docs/personal-panels.md`): one plugin shape; an installed panel runs only in the frame realm; never relax the compiler's import list at display time; the Firstmate never writes the panels switch.
